newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - June 11.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
-- ELECTRICITY COMPANIES WIN TEST CASE OVER PENSIONS

A UK High Court judge has ruled that National Grid and National Power were justified in using pension fund surpluses for large-scale redundancy packages. Pensions ombudsman Julian Farrand had accused National Grid of misusing withdrawals of 75 million sterling and National Power of acting unlawfully by using 300 million stg of surplus from the industry's central fund.
-- US UTILITY MAY MAKE 3.6 BLN STG BID FOR ENERGY

PacifiCorp of the US has entered talks with Britain's electricity and coal company, Energy Group, leading to speculation that a 3.6 million sterling takeover bid for the UK company could take place. The Energy Group has postponed the release of its interim results which were due on Thursday, signalling that an offer could be imminent. Energy Group is being advised by Lazard Brothers and Morgan Stanley, while PacifiCorp is advised by Goldman Sachs.
-- BA COULD SCRAP US LINK PLAN IF APPROVAL IS DELAYED

Robert Ayling, the chief executive of British Airways has announced that if European regulators do not approve the merger between BA and American Airlines by November, the alliance will be dropped. Ayling will continue to press for the alliance which has been under review for one year, held up by elections in the UK and US, but believes if no deal is reached by November it will be more difficult to allocate take-off and landing slots for summer 1998.
-- SURFERS PAY FOR ONLINE ECONOMIST

UK financial news weekly the Economist is to become the first British mainstream publication to go against common Internet practice by charging for online access to its articles. While eight articles per week will remain free, the remainder of the weekly will be provided only if the subscription rate of 48 dollars is paid. The service also includes a searchable archive of back issues and classified advertising.
-- BROWN TO CUT VAT ON "GREEN" PRODUCTS

In the July UK budget, Chancellor Gordon Brown is expected to cut the value-added tax on energy saving goods such as insulation products and draught-proofing materials from 17.5 percent to eight percent, following up on Labour election pledges to adopt environmentally- friendly policies by encouraging households to save fuel. The measure is hoped to offset another VAT cut by Brown on fuel from eight percent to five percent.
-- DAIRY CHIEF WARNS OF INDUSTRY SHAKE-UP

Northern Foods, the largest British dairy company, has declared that a shake-out of the industry has begun, and consumers and retailers should prepare for further restructuring, including the halving of large milk processors in the UK from six to three. Chris Haskins of Northern said there was too much capacity in the industry, with consolidation and mergers taking place worldwide between farmer-owned milk processors.
-- BRUSSELS EXPRESSES DOUBTS OVER FERRY MERGER

Following a study into the proposed merger between ferry companies P&O and Stena Line, the European commission has ruled that the merger can only take place if the resulting company is operated independently of its parent groups' other businesses. While ferry companies remain optimistic that the deal will go through, the commission has expressed doubts about the proposed joint venture.
-- INSTITUTIONS ATTACK NATWEST PERFORMANCE

Institutional investors are continuing to express criticism towards National Westminster Bank over the poor performance of its shares over the past two years, as prices at the Bank have underperformed the rest of the UK sector by 25 percent in the year alone. NatWest has been discussing a merger with Abbey National, but the shareholders insist it is not the size and mix of NatWest's businesses that is the problem, but how those businesses are managed.
-- SOCO IN MONGOLIAN DISCOVERY

UK oil and gas exploration company Soco International has announced a fourth oil discovery in Mongolia, leading to a 20.5p rise in its share prices to 256p. Ed Story, Soco president and chief executive named the discovery of the free flowing oil well a milestone in Mongolia's history, and added that the company's plans included completion of the four discovery wells this summer and installation of production facilities.
-- SR GENT ACCEPTS 31M STG TAKEOVER

SR Gent, the company that provides clothing to retailer Marks and Spencer, has announced that losses at the company have led to its acceptance of a 30.6m stg takeover bid from Prospero Investments. Adrian Olud, a director at Indonesian-based Prospero, said the bid was made due to recent declarations by M&S that it was looking to extend operations into continental Europe and Asia, representing a "significant overlap" with the interests of Polysindo Eka, the polyester manufacturing subsidiary of Prospero.
